status_summary: On icebreakers, Public Law 119-21 (enacted 2025-07-04) funds Coast Guard icebreakers, which a Coast Guard release lists as 4.3 billion dollars for Polar Security Cutters, 3.5 billion dollars for Arctic Security Cutters and 816 million dollars for lighter icebreaking cutters; a presidential memorandum of 2025-10-08 authorized up to four Arctic Security Cutters to be built abroad, and the Coast Guard awarded contracts for 11 Arctic Security Cutters on 2025-12-29 and 2026-02-11, with first delivery expected in 2028. On NATO, the alliance launched Arctic Sentry on 2026-02-11, a coordinating label for existing national Arctic exercises under one command, not a published strategy. On Greenland, the President withdrew threatened tariffs on European countries on 2026-01-21 while announcing a framework with NATO's Secretary-General, and on 2026-09-22 signed with Denmark and Greenland a security agreement providing for two new US bases and investment screening that excludes investors outside NATO, NATO partners and the EU from sensitive sectors. These Greenland actions centre on security and an acquisition push, which goes beyond the Mandate's call to enhance economic ties; no measure expanding US-Greenland trade or investment was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was enacted; a Coast Guard headquarters release of the same day lists 4.3 billion dollars for Polar Security Cutters, 3.5 billion dollars for Arctic Security Cutters and 816 million dollars for light and medium icebreaking cutters.
timeline.source: US Coast Guard release (reprinted by Seapower)

timeline.event: A presidential memorandum authorized up to four Arctic Security Cutters to be built abroad for up to four years, and required a Coast Guard plan within 60 days to phase construction to build domestic expertise.
Finland and the US signed an icebreaker collaboration memorandum at the White House, building on the ICE Pact among the US, Canada and Finland.

The Coast Guard announced contracts for up to six Arctic Security Cutters: up to two from Rauma Marine Constructions in Finland and up to four from Bollinger Shipyards in Louisiana, with first deliveries expected in 2028 (Finland) and 2029 (US).

The President withdrew a threatened tariff on Denmark and seven other European countries tied to his push to acquire Greenland, and announced a framework of a future deal with NATO's Secretary-General covering Arctic security and minerals, without published details.

The Coast Guard completed contract awards for 11 Arctic Security Cutters with an award to Davie Defense for up to five (two at Helsinki Shipyard, three in the US); the first is expected in early 2028.

NATO's Secretary-General announced Arctic Sentry, bringing existing national Arctic exercises under one command coordinated through NATO's Norfolk headquarters; it involves no permanent deployment and is not described as a strategy.

The US, Denmark and Greenland signed a security agreement in New York providing for two new US bases, reaffirming Danish sovereignty and barring investors from outside NATO, NATO partners and the EU from control of sensitive sectors, with Greenland screening investments; it takes effect after approval by the Greenland and Danish parliaments.
